existing_programme.title: Remediate disclaimed audit opinion (Forvis Mazars LLP, year ended 2024-03-31)
existing_programme.rationale: External auditor issued a DISCLAIMED opinion on financial statements. Concerns: Disclaimer of opinion for 2023/24 issued by Forvis Mazars — inherited backstop disclaimer regime affecting most local authorities + Calderdale-specific delay in finalising the 2023/24 and 2024/25 Draft Accounts; One significant deficiency in internal control noted by Forvis Mazars in 2023/24 Annual Report (delivered February 2025); Significant weaknesses in arrangements (VfM) identified in prior years. Direct savings: PSAA scale fee normalisation (current scale fee £250K + disclaimer surcharge). Indirect: lifting MHCLG governance flag reduces borrowing-cost premium (typically 5-15bp on new external debt) + opens £M of grant programmes that require unmodified opinions. Foundation requirement before ANY other transformation saving is credible to auditor or DLUHC.

existing_programme.title: HNSG Reform Plan submission — secures £15.3M DSG write-off (90% of £17.0M)
existing_programme.rationale: DSG cumulative high-needs deficit £17.0M. Under the new High Needs Stability Grant (HNSG) announced 9 Feb 2026, government will write off 90% (~£15.3M) of every council's DSG deficit at 31 March 2026 via Section 31 grant paid Autumn 2026 — CONDITIONAL on the council submitting an approved Local SEND Reform Plan to DfE by 19 June 2026. The £1.7M residual remains on council books. Safety Valve programme closed 1 April 2026 and is folded into HNSG. Statutory override extended to 31 March 2028; gov has committed to absorb all DSG deficits from 1 April 2028 onwards. The savings range below covers (a) plan-submission cost avoidance + (b) residual 10% in-year demand management.
existing_programme.delivery_horizon: 19 June 2026 plan submission deadline; Autumn 2026 grant payment

existing_programme.title: Agency / locum staff demand reduction (£17M concentrated)
existing_programme.rationale: £17M of agency-staff spend across 2 master vendors. Top: REED SPECIALIST RECRUITMENT LTD (£13M), MATRIX SCM LTD (£3M). Standard transformation: cap agency premium at 20% above substantive rate, workforce-plan permanent conversion (6-9 month payback), regional bank pool, open-book master-vendor margins. CIPFA experience: 8-15% reduction in 12-18 months.

existing_programme.title: Energy procurement via CCS / LASER / NEPO frameworks (£15M baseline)
existing_programme.rationale: £15M utility spend across 5 suppliers. Top: NPOWER (£10M), E.ON ENERGY SOLUTIONS T/A EON HIGHWAYS LIGHTING (£2M), SSE CONTRACTING LTD C/O TESGL LTD (£1M), LEONARD CHESHIRE FOUNDATION (£1M), ROSSE SYSTEMS LTD (£1M). Crown Commercial RM6306 + LASER / NEPO consortium flex purchase typically saves 4-8% vs direct supplier contracts on a 3-yr horizon. Plus solar PV self-generation on council estate (7-9 yr payback) + DESNZ Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme grants up to 100% capex on heat pump conversion.

existing_programme.title: Treasury management + borrowing cost optimisation (CFR proxy £1305M)
existing_programme.rationale: Annual revenue £1631M implies indicative CFR c. £1305M. Standard levers: internal borrowing from earmarked reserves, PWLB Certainty Rate trade, MMF counterparty restructuring, LGPS Property Investment Pool inclusion. 10-30bp saving on external debt typical from a fresh review.

existing_programme.title: LGPS employer contribution opportunity (2025 triennial valuation cycle)
existing_programme.rationale: Indicative pay bill £652M × c. 22% employer contribution rate = £144M annual employer contribution. Most LGPS funds materially over-funded post-2022 (returns 2022-25 averaged 7-10% pa vs 3-4% discount-rate assumption). 2025 triennial valuation typically yields 2-4pp employer-rate reduction over 2026-2029. Confirm with administering authority + actuary.

existing_programme.title: Fees, charges + traded-services income optimisation (£163M base)
existing_programme.rationale: Indicative fees & charges + traded-services income c. 10% of revenue = £163M. Standard levers: annual CPI uplift discipline, full-cost-recovery audit on discretionary services (parking, planning, licensing, sports, adult learning, property hire), commercial pricing on traded services. LGA experience: 5-15% income uplift sustainable over 2-3 years.

existing_programme.title: Insurance retention + premium review (£1.6M premium estimate)
existing_programme.rationale: Indicative insurance premium £1.6M (10bp of revenue). Standard 3-5 yr renewal cycle. Levers: tender via IPG / RM Partners (10-25% premium reduction typical), retention review (increase excess + build risk-fund reserve). London-borough cohort average 12% premium reduction at last tender.

existing_programme.title: Contracts Finder portfolio review (43 notices; 4 contracts at £10M+ ceiling)
existing_programme.rationale: Contracts Finder data: 43 notices (21 awarded, £55M aggregate ADVERTISED CEILING value, 0% SME). IMPORTANT: advertised contract value is a CEILING set to avoid retender risk under PCR 2015 Reg.72 / Procurement Act 2023 s.31 — actual spend through the awardee is typically 30-70% of ceiling, with some off-contract ledger spend permitted within the 50%/50% modification limits. 4 contracts at £10M+ ceiling totalling £53M (ceiling, NOT spend) — top 3: All Age Domiciliary Care (ceiling £14M); Approved Provider List for Domiciliary Care for Older People (ceiling £14M); Concession Contract for the Supply of Enforcement Agent Serv (ceiling £13M). Matched against ledger: Supply & Installation of Stairlifts — ceiling £1.5M, actual ledger spend with awardee £2.0M; Supply of Swimwear & Swimming Accessories — ceiling £0.1M, actual ledger spend with awardee £0.1M; Pathway Leaving Care Service — ceiling £4.3M, actual ledger spend with awardee £2.6M. Aggregate identified actual spend £387M. SME-awarded share 0% is below the Procurement Reform 2023 / PPN 03/24 ambition (33% SME share by value). Standard procurement-data savings levers (% of ACTUAL ledger spend, not ceiling): (a) modification-history scrutiny under PCR 2015 Reg.72, (b) Procurement Act 2023 s.31 contract change notice review, (c) re-tender benchmark vs CCS framework rates on next renewal. 2-8% on actual spend through major contracts is a defensible upper bound.

existing_programme.title: Companies House compliance follow-up (£45M flagged — 0 overdue, 2 dissolved, 1 insolvency-history)
existing_programme.rationale: Companies House lookup on top-50 suppliers identified £45M of spend with statutory-compliance flags: £0M to suppliers with overdue accounts (0), £34M to dissolved-status companies (2), £11M to companies with insolvency history (1). NOTE: Some matches are CH fuzzy-search false positives (e.g. school, government-body name collisions) and need human verification. After verification, real flags = (a) credit-risk review on overdue accounts, (b) contract-cleanup on dissolved entities (records still on ledger but supplier extinct — risk of duplicate-payment leakage), (c) PCR 2015 Reg.57 discretionary exclusion review on insolvency-history suppliers in active contracts.

existing_programme.title: Refund / credit-note management + contract dispute resolution (£30M, 26,135 rows)
existing_programme.rationale: 26,135 negative-amount rows totalling £30M — refunds, credit notes, contract reversals. Volume signals correct ledger capture, but proactive levers exist: (a) contract management review on top recurring refund counterparties, (b) duplicate-payment pre-detection, (c) energy-bill credit-management automation. Typical 5-10% reduction in refund volume + faster reconciliation = 10-30bp net cash improvement.

existing_programme.title: Rebuild general reserves to ≥4 months (Critical → Adequate)
existing_programme.rationale: Reserves at 1.5 months (Critical per CIPFA Resilience benchmark). Direction: declining. A 4-month minimum is the CIPFA / S151 prudence floor; below this triggers external auditor VFM concern and elevates s.114 risk.

existing_programme.title: Investigate £68M in flagged split-payment patterns
existing_programme.rationale: DOGE flagged £68M across 0 split-payment instances. Split payments often indicate (a) below-procurement-threshold ledger fragmentation circumventing PCR 2015 Reg.4 contract-value-aggregation rule; or (b) legitimate sub-line invoice splits. Sample audit + reclassify; misuse triggers Reg. 99 challenge exposure.
